Research what real 2b2t-style Minecraft "anarchy" servers actually run, as of August 2026. This is for a hosting company building a one-click "anarchy" preset on itzg/docker-minecraft-server.

Answer concretely and cite sources (URLs):

1. Is "anarchy" a plugin, or just a server config/policy? Confirm definitively. What does 2b2t itself run (it's known to run a heavily modified Paper/Spigot fork — find current public info), and what do typical smaller anarchy servers (e.g. 9b9t, constantiam, 6b6t) run?

2. What EXACT server.properties values define an anarchy preset? Give the concrete list with values: pvp, white-list, enforce-whitelist, spawn-protection, difficulty, hardcore, allow-nether, allow-flight, online-mode, enable-command-block, max-players, view-distance, simulation-distance, player-idle-timeout, gamemode, force-gamemode, level-type/generator-settings, spawn-monsters, etc. Note keepInventory is a gamerule (in level.dat / /gamerule), NOT server.properties -- confirm and explain how itzg's image can set gamerules if at all.

3. What Paper-specific config tweaks (paper-global.yml / paper-world-defaults.yml / spigot.yml / bukkit.yml) do real anarchy servers use? Specifically research:
   - anti-xray (engine-mode) - do anarchy servers use it or disable it?
   - chunk/entity limits to survive lag machines and chunk-ban attacks
   - `book-size` limits / book exploit (Paper's `max-book-page-size`, `max-book-total-size-multiplier`) as chunk-ban / crash protection
   - packet limiter (Paper's `packet-limiter` settings), `incoming-packet-threshold`
   - entity collision / max entity cramming
   - `alt-item-despawn-rate`, `hopper` settings, redstone implementation (`vanilla` vs `alternate-current`) for lag machines
   - Any "unsupported-settings" like allow-permanent-block-break-exploits / allow-piston-duplication / allow-headless-pistons -- do anarchy servers ENABLE duping on purpose? This is important: anarchy culture often WANTS duping.
   - view-distance and no-tick-view-distance
4. What plugins are genuinely typical on an anarchy server? Research whether any of these are real and maintained TODAY: an "Exploit Fixer"-type plugin, anti-crash/anti-lag-machine plugins, "NoChatReports" (is it client-only or is there a server-side plugin/mod?), chunk-ban protection. Give exact plugin names and where they're hosted (SpigotMC ID / Modrinth slug / GitHub). Verify each via https://api.spiget.org/v2/resources/<ID> or https://api.modrinth.com/v2/project/<slug> using curl and report name/downloads/last-update. Be honest if a candidate is dead or sketchy.
5. Does anarchy typically mean NO anticheat? Confirm the cultural norm.
6. Practical hosting warnings: what breaks an anarchy server (lag machines, world size / disk growth, no /home no economy, griefing at spawn, need for a large world border or none, backups).

Return a concise, concrete, well-sourced text report. Do NOT write any files.

## How It Works

Chunk banning is an act of making a chunk or area have too much data for servers to send to the client, so it is forced to kick you off the server if you are near enough to the chunk ban. It works by overloading a specific area with massive amounts of NBT (named binary tag) data. When a player tries to enter the area, the server attempts to send all local data to their computer. Because the data exceeds the network limit, the connection breaks, and the player is kicked.

There are two methods of chunk banning; the first is the method of building high NBT structures, although this does not work in recent versions. # Anarchy Minecraft server preset — research report (Aug 2026)

## 1. Is "anarchy" a plugin? No — it is a **policy + config**, with plugins added *defensively*

**Definitive: there is no "anarchy plugin" that makes a server anarchy.** Anarchy is defined by what you *don't* do: no whitelist, no rules, no bans for cheating, no world resets, no admin intervention, no grief rollbacks. The plugins that real anarchy servers run exist to *survive* that policy (crash/exploit protection), not to create it.

**What 2b2t runs:** Wikipedia states 2b2t runs **modified PaperMC**, on MC **1.21.4** with Bedrock cross-play as of Dec 2025. The fork is private/closed — Hausemaster has never published it, and no public repo exists. Ping data shows a **Velocity** proxy in front (queue server + main server). Notable: 2b2t has **no meaningful anticheat**; the historic NoCom (2018–2021, ~2TB of harvested coordinates, patched 2021-07-15) and RANDAR (patched on 2b2t 2023-08-14) exploits went unfixed for years. As of Aug 2025 2b2t was **forced by Mojang to add an Xbox-community-guidelines chat filter** — a rules concession.

**Smaller servers:** They run **stock Paper (or Purpur/Folia) + a small plugin stack**, not custom forks. AnarchyExploitFixes' own README lists its users: `constantiam.net`, `6b6t.org`, `5b5t.org`, `openanarchy.org`, `10b10t.com`, `4v4d.org`, `endcrystal.me`, and ~20 more. Constantiam is on 1.12.2 and is regarded as the most technically stable of the large ones. **Paper is the correct base for your preset** — Spigot lacks the exploit patches and config surface, and vanilla will not survive contact with an anarchy playerbase.

Sources: [Wikipedia 2b2t](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2b2t) · [AnarchyExploitFixes README (server list)](https://github.com/xGinko/AnarchyExploitFixes) · [Minecraft-Anarchy/anarchy-servers](https://github.com/Minecraft-Anarchy/anarchy-servers)

---

## 2. server.properties — the concrete anarchy preset

All of these map to itzg env vars (confirmed: [itzg server.properties docs](https://docker-minecraft-server.readthedocs.io/en/latest/configuration/server-properties/)).

| property | value | itzg ENV | why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pvp` | `true` | `PVP` | non-negotiable |
| `white-list` | `false` | `ENABLE_WHITELIST` | anyone joins |
| `enforce-whitelist` | `false` | `ENFORCE_WHITELIST` | |
| `spawn-protection` | `0` | `SPAWN_PROTECTION` | **critical** — spawn must be griefable; default 16 breaks the culture |
| `difficulty` | `hard` | `DIFFICULTY` | 2b2t is permanently hard |
| `hardcore` | `false` | `HARDCORE` | anarchy ≠ hardcore; hardcore bans you on death |
| `allow-nether` | `true` | `ALLOW_NETHER` | nether highways are the core travel mechanic |
| `allow-flight` | `true` | `ALLOW_FLIGHT` | see note below |
| `online-mode` | `true` | `ONLINE_MODE` | see warning §6 |
| `enable-command-block` | `false` | `ENABLE_COMMAND_BLOCK` | cmd blocks = instant server takeover |
| `max-players` | `60`–`200` | `MAX_PLAYERS` | above ~100 you need a Velocity queue |
| `view-distance` | `4`–`6` | `VIEW_DISTANCE` | 2b2t-style; low is *the* anarchy norm |
| `simulation-distance` | `4` | `SIMULATION_DISTANCE` | biggest single TPS lever |
| `player-idle-timeout` | `0`, or `20`–`30` with a queue | `PLAYER_IDLE_TIMEOUT` | AFK camping is normal; kick only if queued |
| `gamemode` | `survival` | `MODE` | |
| `force-gamemode` | `true` | `FORCE_GAMEMODE` | stops creative leaking back in |
| `level-type` | `minecraft:normal` | `LEVEL_TYPE` | vanilla generation is the point |
| `generator-settings` | *(empty)* | `GENERATOR_SETTINGS` | |
| `spawn-monsters` | `true` | `SPAWN_MONSTERS` | |
| `max-world-size` | `29999984` (vanilla max) | `MAX_WORLD_SIZE` | 2b2t's border is 30M blocks |
| `enable-rcon` | `true` | `ENABLE_RCON` | required for gamerules, see below |
| `sync-chunk-writes` | `false` | | large perf win on big worlds |

**`allow-flight=true` is counterintuitive but correct.** Vanilla's flight kick is a crude anticheat that false-positives constantly on elytra + high latency, and there's a known boat-kick exploit tied to it. AEF's own optimization guide recommends enabling flight. On a no-anticheat server it protects nothing anyway.

### keepInventory — you are right, it is a gamerule, not server.properties

`keepInventory` lives in `level.dat` (`Data.GameRules`), set via `/gamerule`. It is **not** a server.properties key and itzg has **no** `KEEP_INVENTORY` env var. itzg's supported mechanism is RCON automation:

```yaml
ENABLE_RCON: "true"
RCON_CMDS_STARTUP: |-
  gamerule keepInventory false
  gamerule doFireTick true
  gamerule announceAdvancements false
  gamerule sendCommandFeedback false
  gamerule disableElytraMovementCheck true
```

Vars: `RCON_CMDS_STARTUP`, `RCON_CMDS_ON_CONNECT`, `RCON_CMDS_ON_DISCONNECT`, `RCON_CMDS_FIRST_CONNECT`, `RCON_CMDS_LAST_DISCONNECT`. Leading `/` is optional; use YAML `|-` for multi-line. ([docs](https://docker-minecraft-server.readthedocs.io/en/latest/configuration/auto-rcon-commands/))

**For an anarchy preset, `keepInventory` must be `false`** — loot drop on death is the entire economy. Set it explicitly anyway so a customer flipping presets doesn't inherit `true`. `announceAdvancements false` matters at scale (chat spam), and `disableElytraMovementCheck true` pairs with `allow-flight`.

---

## 3. Paper config — the part that actually keeps the server alive

### anti-xray → **disable it**
Default in `paper-world-defaults.yml` is already `anticheat.anti-xray.enabled: false`. **Leave it off.** Anarchy servers assume everyone uses X-ray (most players run hacked clients); engine-mode 2/3 costs real CPU and causes client FPS drops for zero cultural benefit. This is one of the few places where the anarchy preset is *cheaper* than a normal server. ([Paper anti-xray docs](https://docs.papermc.io/paper/anti-xray/))

### Book / chunk-ban protection — the highest-value setting on the list
The dominant griefing weapon is the **area ban**: a shulker box stuffed with books full of invisible Unicode, dropped as an item entity. It exceeds the network packet limit and kicks every player who comes within ~32 blocks (Paper) / 96 blocks (vanilla). ([minecraft.wiki Tutorial:Chunk ban](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial:Chunk_ban))

`spigot.yml` (Paper's Book-Size-Limits patch, exposed here):
```yaml
settings:
  book-size:
    page-max: 2560          # tighten to 1024 for aggressive protection
    total-multiplier: 0.98  # clamped 0.3–1.0; lower = stricter
```
`paper-global.yml`:
```yaml
item-validation:
  book: { author: 8192, page: 16384, title: 8192 }   # defaults — LOWER these
  lore-line: 8192
```
Recommend `page: 2048`, `author: 256`, `title: 128`. Note **Paper/Purpur already blunt the classic area ban**; vanilla and Fabric do not — another reason the preset must be Paper.

### Packet limiter (`paper-global.yml`)
```yaml
packet-limiter:
  all-packets: { action: KICK, interval: 7.0, max-packet-rate: 500.0 }
  kick-message: "<red><lang:disconnect.exceeded_packet_rate>"
  overrides:
    minecraft:place_recipe: { action: KICK, interval: 7.0, max-packet-rate: 500.0 }
spam-limiter:
  incoming-packet-threshold: 300
  tab-spam-increment: 1
  tab-spam-limit: 500
  recipe-spam-increment: 1
  recipe-spam-limit: 20
misc:
  max-joins-per-tick: 3    # default 5; lower resists join-flood
```
Keep these **at or below** default. Anarchy players run auto-crafters and packet spammers; `place_recipe` (the autorecipe lag exploit) is the one AEF also independently rate-limits.

### Chunk & entity limits (`paper-world-defaults.yml`)
```yaml
chunks:
  auto-save-interval: 6000            # AEF guide's recommendation
  delay-chunk-unloads-by: 5s          # down from 10s
  max-auto-save-chunks-per-tick: 8    # down from 24 — avoids save-freeze stalls
  entity-per-chunk-save-limit:
    experience_orb: 50                # default -1 = unlimited; XP-orb bombs are a classic lag machine
    snowball: 20
    ender_pearl: 20
    arrow: 32
    fireball: 10
    small_fireball: 10
  prevent-moving-into-unloaded-chunks: true
collisions:
  max-entity-collisions: 2            # default 8 — entity cramming is the #1 lag machine
  fix-climbing-bypassing-cramming-rule: true
entities:
  spawning:
    alt-item-despawn-rate:
      enabled: true                   # despawn cobblestone/netherrack/sand fast
      items: { COBBLESTONE: 300, NETHERRACK: 300, SAND: 300, DIRT: 300, GRAVEL: 300 }
    per-player-mob-spawns: true
hopper:
  cooldown-when-full: true
  disable-move-event: true            # big TPS win, safe with no economy plugins
misc:
  redstone-implementation: ALTERNATE_CURRENT
  update-pathfinding-on-block-update: false
```
Also set `bukkit.yml` → `spawn-limits` low (monsters 30, animals 8) and `ticks-per.monster-spawns: 4`.

`redstone-implementation: ALTERNATE_CURRENT` deserves a call-out: default is `VANILLA`, and Alternate Current is dramatically faster on the large redstone contraptions anarchy players build as deliberate lag machines. It is **not** 100% behaviour-identical on exotic circuits — acceptable trade for a hosting preset, but document it.

Set `bukkit.yml` → `autosave: -1` and let Paper's `auto-save-interval` own saving; Bukkit's saver freezes the server on huge maps.

### unsupported-settings — **yes, anarchy servers deliberately enable duping**
This is the culturally load-bearing part. `paper-global.yml`:
```yaml
unsupported-settings:
  allow-headless-pistons: true
  allow-permanent-block-break-exploits: true
  allow-piston-duplication: true
  allow-unsafe-end-portal-teleportation: true
  skip-tripwire-hook-placement-validation: true
  perform-username-validation: false   # only if you intend cracked/odd names
```
- `allow-permanent-block-break-exploits` → bedrock breaking, end portal frame breaking. **Bedrock breaking is a defining anarchy activity** (nether roof access).
- `allow-piston-duplication` → TNT/carpet/rail duping (not sand).
- `allow-headless-pistons` → the tool used to break permanent blocks.

Paper explicitly disclaims support when these are on. Your preset must surface that: **"this preset enables settings PaperMC will not support."** 6b6t goes further and runs community-funded **72-hour "Dupe Events"** — duping is a *marketed feature*, not a bug. Note the practical cost: enabling duping accelerates item-entity counts and therefore disk and lag.

In `paper-world-defaults.yml` → `unsupported-settings.fix-invulnerable-end-crystal-exploit: false` if you want full crystal-PvP parity with 2b2t.

Sources: [Paper global config reference](https://docs.papermc.io/paper/reference/global-configuration/) · [Paper world config reference](https://docs.papermc.io/paper/reference/world-configuration/) · [PaperMC issue #3854 "TNT Duping or Bedrock Breaking? READ ME"](https://github.com/PaperMC/Paper/issues/3854)

### view-distance / no-tick-view-distance
Modern Paper replaced `no-tick-view-distance` with the server.properties split of `view-distance` (send) vs `simulation-distance` (tick). Use `view-distance: 6` / `simulation-distance: 4`. Also cap per-player chunk rates in `paper-global.yml` — this is what stops one elytra-flying player from stalling everyone:
```yaml
chunk-loading-basic:
  player-max-chunk-load-rate: 30.0        # default 100
  player-max-chunk-generate-rate: 8.0     # default -1 (unlimited!) — MUST be capped
  player-max-chunk-send-rate: 40.0        # default 75
chunk-loading-advanced:
  auto-config-send-distance: true
  player-max-concurrent-chunk-loads: 4
  player-max-concurrent-chunk-generates: 2
```
`player-max-chunk-generate-rate: -1` by default is the single most dangerous default for an anarchy server — elytra+firework travel at 60+ blocks/sec generating fresh terrain is both the TPS killer and the disk-growth engine.

## 5. Anticheat — the cultural norm is "none", but the honest answer is nuanced

**No anticheat is the norm, and it is a selling point, not an omission.** Using hacked clients is *normalized* on anarchy — beyond brand-new players, it's rare to find anyone not running one; they're needed for automated travel, PvP, and basic QoL. 2b2t has no real anticheat; cheat clients are openly catalogued on its wiki.

The nuance worth putting in your preset docs: many established anarchy servers **do** keep a minimal, crash-oriented layer — blocking extreme speed hacks and instant-nukers that break thousands of blocks, because those are *server-stability* problems, not fairness problems. The line is: **anything that only advantages a player is allowed; anything that hurts the server is blocked.** That's precisely what Surf/AEF do, and why they are not "anticheat" in the anarchy sense. Servers advertising "NO ANTI CHEAT" at all (e.g. 75b75t) exist as a stricter subgenre.

**Do not ship a preset with GrimAC/NCP/Matrix/Vulcan.** It would be mis-sold.

Sources: [2b2t Wiki: Cheat Clients](https://2b2t.miraheze.org/wiki/Cheat_Clients) · [Wikipedia 2b2t](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2b2t)

## 6. Practical hosting warnings

**🔴 Mojang can blacklist your customer's server — this happened last month.** On **2026-07-15 Mojang added `6b6t.org` to the official blocked-server list**, after (per 6b6t) 2b2t, Purity Vanilla and OldFrog were pressured into adding restrictions. The block happens at the **Mojang session/auth layer**, so the machine stays up but vanilla clients cannot connect; 6b6t's answer was to ship a Fabric bypass mod. 2b2t survived only by adding an Xbox-guidelines chat filter in Aug 2025. **This is a material commercial risk you must disclose in the preset's terms** — a customer can lose their entire playerbase overnight through no fault of your infrastructure, and it is not something you can fix. Consider requiring a chat filter, or at minimum an explicit acknowledgement. Tracking: [sudofox/mojang-blocklist](https://github.com/sudofox/mojang-blocklist) · [6b6t's own writeup](https://blog.6b6t.org/minecraft-banned-6b6t/)

**🔴 Disk growth is the business risk.** 2b2t's world is **~80–100 TB** after ~16 years. At a much smaller scale, ~50 concurrent players grow a world **30–50 GB/month** — because elytra travel generates permanent new region files that are never reclaimed (no world resets, by definition). Implications:
- Never sell an anarchy preset on a fixed small disk without a hard quota and an alert at 70/85%.
- `max-world-size` is your only real lever. 30M blocks is authentic; **offer a 100k–1M block border as the sane default** and let customers opt into bigger.
- Budget for `region/`, `entities/`, and `poi/` all growing together.
- Chunk *generation* rate caps (§3) are the throttle on this.

**🔴 Backups are hard and get harder.** Incremental/rsync-style backup of millions of small `.mca` files degrades badly; full snapshots become impossible past a few hundred GB. Use **ZFS snapshots + send/recv**, not tar. Note the AEF guide's warning: Bukkit's autosave freezes the server on large maps — set `bukkit.yml: autosave: -1` and use Paper's interval saver, and take snapshots from a quiesced/save-off window. There is no rollback culture on anarchy, so backups are **disaster recovery only**, never grief recovery — never advertise otherwise.

**🟠 Lag machines are intentional and constant.** Players build them as weapons. Beyond §3 config: `armor-stands-tick: false` (AEF guide's explicit recommendation), cap `experience_orb` per chunk, and set `max-entity-collisions: 2`. Expect deliberate TPS attacks — your monitoring must not treat sustained low TPS as a platform fault.

**🟠 Spawn is a wasteland by design.** Spawn will be lava-cast, obsidian-walled, and trapped within days. `spawn-protection: 0` is required. New players will die repeatedly at spawn — that's the product. Consider suggesting a spawn-radius randomizer plugin *only* as an opt-out.

**🟠 No `/home`, no `/tpa`, no economy, no land claim.** These are the single most common support tickets and the most common way a "anarchy" preset gets ruined. Ship the preset with **zero** utility plugins — no EssentialsX, no WorldGuard, no CoreProtect, no LuckPerms beyond console. Document that adding them makes it not-anarchy.

**🟠 Griefing generates support tickets you must refuse.** Write the policy into the product page: no rollbacks, no item restoration, no bans on request. Otherwise your support team absorbs the cost of the customer's game design.

**🟡 Network-layer attacks.** Anarchy servers attract Minecraft-protocol DDoS (handshake spam, MOTD flood, login flood) that generic UDP scrubbing does not stop. Wants: L4 TCP filtering, per-IP connection limits (3–5 simultaneous), `max-joins-per-tick: 3`. If you front with Velocity/Bungee, **`server-ip=127.0.0.1` on the backend is mandatory** — an exposed backend with proxy-forwarding enabled is a trivial full-server takeover (auth bypass, spoof any UUID including operators). This is the #1 real-world anarchy server backdoor.

**🟡 Version choice.** Current MC is **26.2** (confirmed via Modrinth/Spiget version tags). Surf and NoChatReports-Spigot cover 26.2; **AnarchyExploitFixes does not** (max 1.21.9). If you want AEF in the stack, pin the preset to **1.21.8/1.21.9**. Otherwise ship 26.x with Surf only. 2b2t itself sat on 1.21.4; 6b6t moved to 1.21.11 — anarchy servers are conservative about versions, so a pinned 1.21.x preset is defensible and arguably more authentic.

**🟡 `online-mode`.** Keep `true`. Cracked (`online-mode=false`) anarchy servers exist, but they invite account spoofing, are unbannable-by-design in the worst way, and expose you to abuse-desk complaints. If you offer a cracked variant, isolate it and require the Velocity `player-info-forwarding-mode` to be locked down.
